PROJECT TITLE
AI-Assisted Climate Resilience for Smallholder Farmers in Maharashtra

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
GreenHarvest Labs proposes to develop and deploy AI-assisted irrigation and soil monitoring tools for smallholder farmers in Maharashtra. This project aims to significantly reduce agricultural water usage and enhance crop yield resilience against the escalating impacts of climate change. By integrating climate tech with sustainable agriculture practices, we seek to empower vulnerable farming communities. We are seeking funding within the range of INR 25 lakh to INR 1 crore to implement this vital initiative.

PROBLEM & NEED
Smallholder farmers in Maharashtra face severe challenges from water scarcity, unpredictable rainfall patterns, and soil degradation exacerbated by climate change. Traditional farming methods often lead to inefficient water use and suboptimal yields, leaving farmers highly vulnerable to economic instability. There is a critical need for accessible, affordable, and effective technological solutions to improve resource management and secure livelihoods.

APPROACH & ACTIVITIES
*   Develop AI models for precise irrigation scheduling based on real-time soil moisture, weather data, and crop needs.
*   Design and deploy low-cost, robust sensor networks for soil health and environmental monitoring.
*   Create an intuitive mobile application for farmers to receive actionable insights and manage their irrigation.
*   Conduct pilot implementations with selected small farmer cohorts, providing hands-on training and support.
*   Iteratively refine the technology based on farmer feedback and performance data.

EXPECTED IMPACT
This project is expected to reduce agricultural water consumption by 25-35%, leading to substantial water savings. Crop yields are projected to increase by 15-20% due to optimized resource allocation and improved soil health. Farmers will experience enhanced climate resilience, reduced input costs, and improved income stability. The initiative will foster sustainable agricultural practices across the region.

BUDGET SUMMARY
We request funding between INR 25 lakh and INR 1 crore. This budget will cover research and development, sensor and software deployment, farmer training programs, project management, and monitoring and evaluation activities.

CONCLUSION
GreenHarvest Labs is committed to leveraging climate tech for a sustainable agricultural future in India. This project offers a scalable and impactful solution to critical challenges faced by smallholder farmers, promising significant environmental and socio-economic benefits. We believe this initiative represents a crucial step towards building resilient farming communities in Maharashtra.
